couplets.label: K1
couplets.question: Underside forewing cell: pair of pale subbasal lines
couplets.a_text: Forewing underside without a pair of pale subbasal lines crossing the discal cell — Pavana group (Four-line Blues)
couplets.b_text: Forewing underside with a pair of pale subbasal lines crossing the discal cell — Berenice / Kurava group (Six-line Blues)
couplets.hint: Hold the forewing to the light and look inside the large closed cell near the wing base. Two pale parallel lines = Six-line Blue (berenice/kurava group). No lines = Four-line Blue (pavana group). This is the primary split for all Nacaduba.

couplets.label: K2
couplets.question: Hindwing underside: prominent black submarginal spot in space 6
couplets.a_text: Hindwing underside with a prominent rounded black submarginal spot in space 6 (near costal margin). FW 14.0–15.5 mm. — Nacaduba angusta
couplets.b_text: Hindwing underside without a prominent submarginal spot in space 6
couplets.hint: In N. angusta the large black spot in HW space 6 is conspicuous and matches a prominent spot in space 2 near the tornus. In all other four-line blues the space-6 spot is absent or very inconspicuous.

couplets.label: K3
couplets.question: Underside postdiscal band: double series with paler space between
couplets.a_text: Postdiscal band composed of a double series of pale striae inwardly bounded by darker lines, with the space between the two striae paler than the ground colour
couplets.b_text: Area between the postdiscal striae unicolorous and of the ground colour (not paler between striae)
couplets.hint: In N. pavana and N. russelli the postdiscal band shows two distinct parallel rows with a noticeably paler gap between them. In N. pactolus, N. hermus, N. subperusia and the larger species the ground colour between the striae is the same as the surrounding wing.

couplets.label: K4
couplets.question: Male upperside: wing colour (double-band species, FW 11–12 mm)
couplets.a_text: ♂ upperside pale greyish blue, border a thread; ♀ upperside brown with wedge-shaped pale blue discal patch on FW and basal blue on HW. FW 11.0–12.0 mm. — Nacaduba pavana
couplets.b_text: ♂ upperside rather pale purple blue, border inwardly diffuse; ♀ as in N. pavana but blue patch darker. FW 11.0–12.0 mm. — Nacaduba russelli
couplets.hint: N. pavana males are a distinctive pale greyish-blue. N. russelli males have a richer, more saturated pale purple-blue. Both species are very similar on the underside — male upperside colour is the primary separating character.

couplets.label: K5
couplets.question: Underside striae character: broad and yellowish vs. narrow
couplets.a_text: Striae broad, diffuse, and distinctly yellowish; postdiscal band almost blended into ground colour. FW 14.5–16.0 mm. — Nacaduba pactolus
couplets.b_text: Striae narrow and well defined, slightly wider in ♀ than in ♂
couplets.hint: N. pactolus has the broadest, most diffuse, and most yellowish striae in the genus — the postdiscal band almost loses its structure. All other four-line blues in this branch (hermus, subperusia, pendleburyi, solta, sanaya, asaga) have cleaner, narrower, whiter striae.

couplets.label: K6
couplets.question: Hindwing underside: spacing between striae in spaces 4 and 5
couplets.a_text: Inner submarginal and outer postdiscal striae in HW spaces 4 and 5 nearly touching (very narrow gap); striae pale buff in ♂, whitish in ♀
couplets.b_text: Inner submarginal and outer postdiscal striae in HW spaces 4 and 5 widely separated — by at least half the width of the postdiscal band
couplets.hint: In N. hermus and N. subperusia the two sets of striae in HW spaces 4–5 are very close and almost touching. In N. pendleburyi, N. solta, N. sanaya and N. asaga the gap between them is conspicuously wide.

couplets.label: K7
couplets.question: Male upperside and HW tornal spot ring colour (spaces 4–5 nearly touching)
couplets.a_text: ♂ upperside violet blue with a slightly frosted appearance (white ribbon scales); border a thread. ♀ upperside pale shining blue with only a very slight purple tinge. HW tornal black spot in space 2 crowned by a brownish-orange ring. FW 13–15 mm. — Nacaduba hermus
couplets.b_text: ♂ upperside violet blue, not frosted; lacks white ribbon scales. HW tornal black spot in space 2 crowned by a clear bright orange ring. FW 13–16 mm. — Nacaduba subperusia
couplets.hint: The ring colour of the HW tornal spot is the most reliable character: dull brownish-orange = hermus; clear bright orange = subperusia. The frosted male upperside from white ribbon scales also diagnoses N. hermus.

couplets.label: K8
couplets.question: Forewing underside: postdiscal band continuous and straight from v3 to v7
couplets.a_text: FW postdiscal band continuous and almost straight from vein 3 to vein 7 on the underside. FW 15–16 mm. — Nacaduba solta
couplets.b_text: FW postdiscal band not continuous and straight — angled, curved inward, or slightly dislocated at vein 6
couplets.hint: N. solta has a notably straight, unbroken postdiscal band running from vein 3 to vein 7. N. pendleburyi, N. sanaya and N. asaga all show curvature or dislocation in this band.

couplets.label: K9
couplets.question: Forewing upperside black border and forewing length
couplets.a_text: FW black border widens appreciably toward the apex on the upperside; inner submarginal and postdiscal striae widely separated in HW spaces 4–5. FW 14–16 mm. — Nacaduba pendleburyi
couplets.b_text: FW black border a narrow thread, not widening toward apex; FW postdiscal band curved inward and slightly dislocated at vein 6. FW 13–16 mm
couplets.hint: N. pendleburyi is the only species in this branch where the FW black border broadens conspicuously toward the apex. N. sanaya (FW 13–14.5 mm, Malay Peninsula) and N. asaga (FW 15–16 mm, Borneo only) both have a curved/dislocated postdiscal band.

couplets.label: K10
couplets.question: Male upperside tint, forewing size and locality
couplets.a_text: ♂ upperside purple with a distinct steely grey tint; or FW 15–16 mm; or specimen from Borneo (Sabah, Sarawak, Brunei). — Nacaduba asaga
couplets.b_text: ♂ upperside purple without a steely grey tint; FW 13–14.5 mm; Malay Peninsula record. — Nacaduba sanaya
couplets.hint: N. asaga is restricted to Borneo and has a distinctive steely grey tint on the male upperside; it is also larger (FW 15–16 mm). N. sanaya occurs on the Malay Peninsula, is smaller (FW 13–14.5 mm), and lacks the steely tint.

couplets.label: K11
couplets.question: Hindwing underside: two large equal orange-ringed spots in spaces 1b and 2
couplets.a_text: Two large equal-sized black spots ringed with orange in HW spaces 1b and 2 near the tornus, both conspicuous and visible by transparency on the upperside. — Nacaduba biocellata
couplets.b_text: Tornal markings not as above — no pair of conspicuous, equal orange-ringed black spots in spaces 1b and 2
couplets.hint: The two striking orange-ringed eye-spots of N. biocellata are unique in the genus — both are large, clearly equal in size, and their orange rings show prominently through the wing membrane on the upperside. In all other six-line blues the tornal area is far more subdued.

couplets.label: K12
couplets.question: Underside: wing bases conspicuously darkened
couplets.a_text: Wing bases (basal area of both wings on the underside) distinctly darker than the rest of the wing, giving a two-toned appearance. — Nacaduba beroe
couplets.b_text: Ground colour relatively even from base to margin; basal area not conspicuously darker
couplets.hint: N. beroe has a noticeably dark basal area on the underside — the contrast with the paler outer wing is clear. In N. kurava, N. berenice, N. calauria and N. kirtoni the underside ground colour is relatively even throughout.

couplets.label: K13
couplets.question: Male upperside: underside markings visible by transparency
couplets.a_text: On the male, underside striae clearly visible by transparency through the wing membrane on the upperside; wings notably translucent. FW 13.5–15 mm. — Nacaduba kurava
couplets.b_text: Upperside appears opaque; underside markings not visible through the wing membrane (or female specimen)
couplets.hint: N. kurava has distinctively translucent wings — the underside pattern shows clearly through on the male upperside. N. berenice, N. calauria and N. kirtoni all have more opaque wings where the underside markings do not show through.

couplets.label: K14
couplets.question: Male upperside: white ribbon scales (frosted sheen)
couplets.a_text: ♂ upperside with abundant white ribbon scales giving a frosted or slightly iridescent sheen. HW tornal spot in space 2 black with metallic green scales and a pale orange halo. FW 11–13 mm. — Nacaduba berenice
couplets.b_text: ♂ upperside deeper purple-blue, without white ribbon scales — or female specimen
couplets.hint: The abundant white ribbon scales of N. berenice give it a subtly shimmery, frosted look compared with the deeper, more uniform purple-blue of N. calauria and N. kirtoni. Assess the discal area in good light. Not applicable to females.

couplets.label: K15
couplets.question: Elevation of record
couplets.a_text: Butterfly recorded at high elevation (above approximately 1200 m); or male genitalia examined and matching N. kirtoni. — Nacaduba kirtoni
couplets.b_text: Lowland to mid-elevation record; ♂ upperside deeper purple-blue, no ribbon scales. — Nacaduba calauria
couplets.hint: N. kirtoni is a highland specialist recorded above 1200 m, nearly identical to N. berenice/calauria on the underside. N. calauria occurs at lower elevations. Reliable distinction of kirtoni from berenice requires male genitalia examination.
